message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|----------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often act as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β₂‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav)
• **Connexins** (gap junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides structural support)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger in red blood cells)
• **Protein kinase C** (binds to phosphatidylserine)
• **Glycophorin A** (red‑cell membrane protein, peripheral) | | **Glycoproteins & glycolipids** | Often involved in cell recognition, signaling, and protection. | • **MHC class I & II molecules** (antigen presentation)
• **CD antigens** (e.g., CD4, CD8)
• **Selectins** (leukocyte adhesion)
• **Heparan sulfate proteoglycans** (growth factor binding) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to membrane lipids (e.g., GPI anchors). | • **CD59** (protectin, GPI‑anchored)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** (some are GPI‑anchored) | ### How to think about plasma‑membrane proteins 1. **Transmembrane vs. peripheral** – Transmembrane proteins cross the bilayer; peripheral proteins sit on the surface or are loosely attached. 2. **Functional groups** – Channels, transporters, pumps, receptors, adhesion molecules, enzymes, structural proteins. 3. **Post‑translational modifications** – Many membrane proteins are glycosylated or lipid‑anchored, which influences their localization and function. These proteins together maintain the cell’s selective permeability, mediate communication with the environment, and provide structural integrity.
